questions.question: The value of (1)/(3-sqrt{8)}-(1)/(sqrt{8)-sqrt{7}}+(1)/(sqrt{7)-sqrt{6}}-(1)/(sqrt{6)-sqrt{5}}+(1)/(sqrt{5)-2} is equal to:
questions.solution:
__**Calculation:**__

We have,

 (1)/(3 - sqrt{8)}=(1)/(3 - sqrt{8)}times frac{3 + sqrt{8}}{3 + sqrt{8}}=3 + sqrt8 

Similarly, we can get

(1)/(sqrt{8)-sqrt{7}}=sqrt{8}+sqrt{7}

(1)/(sqrt{7)-sqrt{6}}=sqrt{7}+sqrt{6}

(1)/(sqrt{6)-sqrt{5}}=sqrt{6}+sqrt{5}

(1)/(sqrt{5)-2}=sqrt{5}+2

On putting these values in the question,

3 + √8 - √8 - √7 + √7 + √6 - √6 - √5 + √5 + 2

⇒ 3 + 2

**⇒ 5**

questions.question: If a 20 m long rope is cut into pieces of 1.6 m each, what percentage of the rope will be left over?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total pieces = 20 ÷ 1.6 = 12.5 pieces.

Full pieces cut = 12. Remainder = 0.5 pieces.

Length of leftover = 0.5 × 1.6 = 0.8 m.

Leftover percentage = (0.8 ÷ 20) × 100 = 4%.

In decimal form, 4% is expressed as 0.04.

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Total length = 20 m, Piece length = 1.6 m.

Formula used: Remainder = Total length − (Number of whole pieces × Length of one piece)

 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 0 m
 19.2 m
 20 m
 12 Full Pieces (1.6 m each)
 Leftover = 0.8 m
 Total Rope Length = 20 m

⇒ Number of complete pieces = 20 ÷ 1.6 = 12.5

⇒ Total pieces = 12 (since only whole pieces are cut)

⇒ Length of 12 pieces = 12 × 1.6 = 19.2 m

⇒ Length of leftover rope = 20 − 19.2 = 0.8 m

⇒ Percentage of leftover = (Leftover ÷ Total Length) × 100

⇒ Percentage = (0.8 ÷ 20) × 100 = 4%

⇒ Expressed in options as a decimal: 4/100 = 0.04

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Decimal

To convert a percentage into a decimal, divide the number by 100. Example: x% = x/100.

Division and Remainder

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder. Here, 20 = (1.6 × 12) + 0.8.

Percentage Change

Percentage change = (Change ÷ Original Value) × 100. This is used to find leftovers or profit/loss ratios.</p

questions.question: Express 4.overline{142} in the form (p)/(q), where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **pure recurring decimal** like N.abc..., the fraction is: (**Whole number** × 999 + **Repeating part**) ÷ 999

Here, the **whole number** is 4 and the **repeating part** is 142.

Numerator = (4 × 999) + 142 = 3996 + 142 = 4138

Denominator = 999 (as 3 digits are repeating)

**∴ The correct answer is 4138/999.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x = 4.142142142...

**Formula Used:** Multiplying by 10ⁿ where n is the number of repeating digits to eliminate the decimal part.

⇒ Let x = 4.142142... ---- (i)

⇒ Multiplying equation (i) by 1000:

⇒ 1000x = 4142.142142... ---- (ii)

⇒ Subtracting equation (i) from equation (ii):

⇒ 1000x − x = 4142.142142... − 4.142142...

⇒ 999x = 4138

⇒ x = 4138/999

**∴ The correct answer is 4138/999.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pure Recurring Decimals

A decimal in which all the figures after the decimal point are repeated. Example: 0.333... = 1/3.

Mixed Recurring Decimals

A decimal in which some figures do not repeat while others do. To convert, subtract non-repeating part from the total number for the numerator.

Rational Number Property

Every **recurring decimal** can be expressed in the form p/q, making it a **rational number**.</p

questions.question: 0.12112111211112 ______ is a number, which is?
questions.solution:
**Explanation** -

The pattern seems to repeat a sequence of numbers: 121, 1211, 12111, and so on, with an additional 2 at the end.

This type of sequence, where each segment extends by adding one more digit to the end, repeating the previous pattern, suggests an irrational number.

Irrational numbers are decimal numbers that neither terminate nor repeat in a specific pattern.

In this case, while there's a repeating structure within the sequence, the addition of a new digit at each step makes it non-repeating and non-terminating, fitting the definition of an irrational number.

**Hence Option (2) is correct.**
